title: The Fool – upright
body_md:
The Fool stands at the cliff's edge with a small bundle and a white rose, eyes lifted to the sky. Waite reads the card as a free spirit setting out without counting the cost. Upright, it finds you at the threshold of a beginning: still naive, still unsure of the terrain, yet that lightness is exactly your advantage.

Watch for impulsiveness and for brushing aside the advice of people who have walked this path. This week, start the new thing you keep postponing because you are "not ready", but bring along one trusted friend to remind you to look where you step.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Magician – upright
body_md:
The Magician stands before a table laid with all four tools: wand, cup, sword and coin, one hand raised to heaven, one pointing to earth. Waite reads the card as skill, diplomacy and will directed toward a goal. Upright, it says you already hold what you need; what is missing is the decision to use it.

Watch for cleverness sliding into trickery, or talking better than you act. This week, list three resources already available to you and put one of them to work on the idea you have carried for a while.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The High Priestess – upright
body_md:
The High Priestess sits between a black and a white pillar, a veil of pomegranates behind her, a scroll resting half-hidden in her lap. Waite calls her secrets, the future still unrevealed, the silent and wise woman. Upright, she asks you to slow down: the answer is not out there yet but beneath the surface, in intuition and in what you already know without admitting it.

Watch for using "let's wait and see" to avoid deciding. This week, before you ask anyone's opinion on the question nagging you, write down what you genuinely feel about it.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Empress – upright
body_md:
The Empress sits among ripe wheat beside a stream, on embroidered cushions, wearing a crown of twelve stars. Waite links her to fruitfulness, initiative, action and long, abundant days. Upright, she speaks of nurture: a project, a relationship or your own body is asking for care so it can grow in its own time.

Watch for overindulgence, or taking all the caretaking onto yourself. This week, do one concrete act of nourishment: cook a proper meal, water the plants, or get three full nights of sleep in a row.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Emperor – upright
body_md:
The Emperor sits on a stone throne carved with rams' heads, sceptre in hand, mountains at his back. Waite reads the card as stability, power, protection and reason. Upright, it says your situation needs structure: clear boundaries, a clear plan, and someone willing to take responsibility.

Watch for rigidity, giving orders instead of listening, or using discipline to hide a fear of losing control. This week, choose one messy area of your life and give it a single simple rule you can actually keep.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Hierophant – upright
body_md:
The Hierophant sits between two pillars, hand raised in blessing, two followers kneeling at his feet. Waite reads the card as alliance, marriage, tradition and the person to whom you turn for guidance. Upright, it suggests learning from what has been tested: teachers, books, rituals, the agreements of a community.

Watch for following something only because "it has always been done this way", or picking the safe template without understanding it. This week, ask someone more experienced about what you are doing, and really listen before you argue.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Lovers – upright
body_md:
Two figures stand bare beneath an angel, the tree of knowledge and the tree of life behind them. Waite reads the card as attraction, love, beauty and trials overcome. Upright, it is not only about a couple but about a choice made from values: what do you pick when heart and reason both speak?

Watch for dodging the decision by letting someone else make it, or mistaking a passing pull for real attachment. This week, write down three values you will not trade away, then hold a pending decision up against them.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Chariot – upright
body_md:
The charioteer stands upright holding no reins, steering a black and a white sphinx by will alone. Waite reads the card as succour, triumph and the strength to overcome obstacles. Upright, it says you have momentum: the opposing pulls inside you can move toward one destination if you keep your hands on the wheel.

Watch for winning at any cost, racing so fast you leave your companions behind, or arrogance after a success. This week, set one small goal with a firm deadline and deliver it on time.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Strength – upright
body_md:
A woman gently closes the lion's jaws, the sign of infinity above her head. Waite assigns the card to power, energy, courage and magnanimity. Upright, it describes a strength unlike force: patience, gentleness and self-command before the wild parts of yourself, such as anger, fear or craving.

Watch for confusing patience with endurance, or holding yourself together so long that nobody notices the strain. This week, when a strong feeling rises, try counting to ten and naming it before you respond.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Hermit – upright
body_md:
The Hermit stands on a snowy peak, raising a lantern that holds a six-pointed star, a staff in his other hand. Waite reads the card as prudence and circumspection. Upright, it invites a deliberate retreat: less noise, less advice, so you can hear your own voice and light the way with the experience you have gathered.

Watch for isolation that drags on, or using "I need time to think" to avoid the people close to you. This week, spend one evening with notifications off, walk alone, and carry exactly one question with you.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Wheel of Fortune – upright
body_md:
The wheel turns in the sky, four creatures reading at the corners, a sphinx seated on top. Waite calls the card destiny, success, elevation and luck. Upright, it says a cycle is shifting: something outside your control is changing direction, often toward the easier side.

Watch for folding your arms and waiting for luck, or forgetting that what rises on the wheel also comes down. This week, prepare one small thing so you can say yes the moment a chance appears: update the file, return the call, clear the space.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Justice – upright
body_md:
Justice sits between two pillars, sword raised in the right hand, scales held in the left. Waite reads the card as equity, rightness, probity and the deserving side prevailing. Upright, it says the results you are receiving reflect what you planted, and that a decision needs weighing by facts rather than sympathy.

Watch for harshness toward others, picking at every small fault, or delaying in search of "perfect fairness". This week, clear up one vague agreement with someone: say plainly what you want and what you will do.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Hanged Man – upright
body_md:
A man hangs by one foot from a living T-shaped tree, his face calm and haloed. Waite describes the card as wisdom, circumspection, sacrifice and intuition. Upright, it speaks of a pause you did not choose: things have stalled, and it is precisely from this inverted angle that you see what was hidden before.

Watch for pointless sacrifice, or enduring only to be seen as the good one. This week, release one task you are forcing to completion and ask: what if I did not do it the old way at all?
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Death – upright
body_md:
A rider in black armour carries a banner with a white rose while the sun rises between two distant towers. Waite reads the card as ending and transformation. Take Death here as a chapter closing to make room for the next: a habit, a role, or a self-image that has passed its use-by date.

Watch for clinging to what is finished out of fear of the gap, which only stretches the transition and makes it harder than it needs to be. This week, make a small ritual of closure: clear the inbox, pack the box away, or write a letter you do not send.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Temperance – upright
body_md:
An angel stands with one foot on land and one in water, pouring liquid back and forth between two cups. Waite reads the card as moderation, economy and skilful management. Upright, it says you are blending two things that seemed opposed: work and rest, reason and feeling, giving and receiving. Mixing patiently in the right measure lasts longer than a burst of effort.

Watch for a middle path so mild it becomes bland, avoiding every clear choice. This week, name one extreme you are leaning toward and deliberately add a little of the other side.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Devil – upright
body_md:
A horned figure squats on a pedestal, two people loosely chained at its feet; the chains are wide enough to slip, yet they stay. Waite assigns the card to force, excess and what feels fated but is not for that reason evil. Upright, it points to a bond you have accepted: a habit, a fear, a relationship or the belief that "I cannot be otherwise".

Watch for blaming circumstances instead of looking at the chain you are holding. This week, name one thing you lean on too heavily and go without it for a single day to see what actually happens.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Tower – upright
body_md:
Lightning knocks the crown from the top of a tower, fire breaks out, two figures fall. Waite reads the card as an unforeseen upheaval that brings down what was built on a false footing. Upright, it speaks of a truth arriving suddenly: a plan, a belief or a self-image no longer holds, and its collapse, however painful, is also a release.

Watch for rushing to rebuild exactly what stood before. This week, if something has just broken apart, write down three things it taught you before you start rebuilding anything.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Star – upright
body_md:
A woman kneels by a pool, pouring water onto the land and into the water, one great star above her among seven smaller ones. Waite records the card as loss and privation but also hope and bright prospects; most readers lean toward the latter. Upright, it arrives after the storm: you are allowed to trust again, to heal, to be unguarded without fear.

Watch for hope that never connects to action. This week, do one small thing for a future you cannot see yet: plant a seed, open a modest savings pot, take the first lesson.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Moon – upright
body_md:
A crescent cradles a full moon, a dog and a wolf howl, a crayfish crawls from the pool onto a long road between two towers. Waite reads the card as illusion, fear, hidden things and error in the dark. Upright, it says you are walking through unclear territory: moods rise and fall, information is missing, imagination colours in the worry.

Watch for making a big decision while your mind is foggy, or believing the worst-case script you drew yourself. This week, take one growing worry and split it: which part is verified fact, which part is your guess?
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The Sun – upright
body_md:
A naked child rides a white horse beneath a blazing sun, sunflowers and a wall behind. Waite assigns the card to material happiness, a contented union and satisfaction. Upright, it is among the brightest cards in the deck: clarity, warmth, vitality and joy that needs no reason.

Watch for complacency, or shining so brightly that you forget who is standing in the shade. This week, do something childlike on purpose: get morning sun on your face, play a game, or praise someone loudly and sincerely.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Judgement – upright
body_md:
An angel sounds a trumpet in the sky; figures rise from their graves with arms open. Waite reads the card as change of position, renewal and outcome. Upright, it speaks of a calling: you are invited to rise out of an old phase, look back over the whole road with forgiving eyes, and choose again who you want to become.

Watch for judging yourself too harshly, or hearing the call and never standing up. This week, write a short review of a chapter that has ended: what is worth keeping, what deserves forgiveness and release.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: The World – upright
body_md:
A dancer floats inside a laurel wreath holding two wands, the four creatures at the corners. Waite reads the card as assured success, recompense, voyage and change of place. Upright, it says a circle has closed: what you pursued has become part of you, and from here the world widens.

Watch for refusing to call something finished so you never have to claim it, or reaching the goal and feeling empty because you skipped the celebration. This week, formally announce one completed thing to at least one person, then allow yourself a full day off.
source_ref: Waite, Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
